A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Multiscale-SGD and Mesh-Free Convolution work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, proofs, tables and figures, support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original gradient-discrepancy experiments, blur-kernel estimation, image denoising and super-resolution results, plus architectural and runtime analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports image deblurring and inpainting experiments, with quantitative scores and reconstructed-image examples.

M1.justification: The multiscale gradient estimator, Full-Multiscale training framework and PDE/FFT-based MFC construction are retained. The main-text super-resolution loss changes from MSE to negative SSIM, but v1 Table 13 already specified SSIM optimization; this resolves inconsistent documentation rather than establishing a changed objective.

E1.justification: v2 adds image deblurring on STL10 and inpainting reported on CelebA, retaining the earlier denoising, Urban100 super-resolution and synthetic experiments. Image deblurring reconstructs images and is distinct from the retained blur-kernel estimation task. Inpainting captions in Figures 12–13 inconsistently name STL10.

E2.justification: The RandomResizedCrop variants of UNet and MFC-UNet compared in v1 Appendix D.7 and Table 11 are removed. Standard-network comparisons and the ESPCN/MFC-ESPCN/FNO-ESPCN comparison remain; extending existing comparators to new tasks does not introduce new comparator methods.

E3.justification: v2 reports equal 250-iteration super-resolution levels and revised architecture specifications, replacing v1's decreasing-level/early-stopping account. It adds deblurring and inpainting protocols, changes reported blur-estimation stopping from test to validation loss, and describes STL10 denoising evaluation as test-set evaluation instead of v1's 512-image validation evaluation.

E4.justification: v1's work-budget convergence analysis, doubled-training experiment and random-crop comparison disappear (Figure 5, Tables 9 and 11). v2 adds deblurring/inpainting qualitative cases. The deeper-network, Fourier-convolution, runtime and feature-map analyses are retained, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report CPU timings averaged over 500 operations. Neither reports training-seed counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests; the revision introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds deblurring/inpainting scores and removes results from the discontinued analyses. Super-resolution results are replaced under revised settings: Full-Multiscale-SGD work rises from 340 to 7,875 WU, and MFC-ESPCN SSIM changes from 0.82 to 0.7866 (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 4). These are not comparable-setting performance changes. Denoising and runtime values are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C corrects an iteration index and adds the equal-iteration work derivation, yielding 63/16 N0I and approximately 3.8-fold savings relative to SGD. Section 2.1 also revises the residual estimator's batch index and index range. The core gradient, convergence and expressivity lemmas and proofs remain.

C1.justification: The four stated contributions remain. The rewritten abstract foregrounds Multiscale-SGD and explicitly qualifies standard-convolution benefits as applying when noise is not significant, narrowing the earlier unqualified empirical statement.

C2.justification: v2 explains that inpainting and super-resolution require more iterations per level, limiting their work savings, and makes the approximately 160-fold speedup statement conditional on optimal implementation. It removes v1's interpretation attributing random-crop degradation to reduced receptive fields. The feature-smoothing explanation and FFT-runtime limitation remain.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands task-specific details: blur-kernel parameters, rectangle-mask generation, explicit batch/iteration quantities, and super-resolution architecture widths and parameter counts. However, it drops the 512-image validation disclosure and super-resolution early-stopping details. Hardware information and the promise to release PyTorch code upon acceptance remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to multigrid, Multilevel Monte Carlo, multiscale CNN training and Fourier neural operators remain the same. Reference formatting and minor wording changes do not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are rewritten, wording is corrected, and experimental and appendix material is reorganized. Blur-estimation details move into Appendix D.1, and runtime discussions are consolidated. Most method/theory prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, redraws Figures 1–2, consolidates benchmark results into a multi-task Table 4, and restructures runtime tables. It relocates the blur-convergence figure, removes discontinued-analysis displays and adds deblurring/inpainting galleries. These substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Broader restoration-task evidence and more explicit settings improve coverage and reproducibility. However, removing budget-based convergence, longer-training and random-crop analyses weakens scrutiny of the central efficiency claim. The settings explaining the differing super-resolution results in v2 Tables 4 and 7 also remain unclear. These competing changes prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
